_meta.design_limits: Installed limits (installed_power_kW, installed_area_m2, max_capacity_tph, installed_burner_kW, installed_drum_volume_m3, max_airflow_m3h): null = to be provided from vendor/design data; the design check reports it as NO LIMIT until filled

CR.5003._note: Upstream of the pivot feed point (spec ch.5: the feed curve is MEASURED downstream of the primary station), so this machine is not wired into the flowsheet. Its parameters are used by the reference-curve calibration script only.

s_CSS.name: Closed-side setting (CSS) - informative only, not used by any computation

SR.5007._purchase_min_note: CLIENT DECISION 2026-08-15 (error-hunt PD-2, option 1 of 3): purchase minima = the RAIN duty, the true worst circumstance (weather rain, 7 % moisture, wet_capacity_factor 0.75 -> engine 9.07/9.53 m2, rounded UP to 9.1/9.6) - full production during rain weeks per the rain-week ruling. The +25 % [H] allowance is NOT stacked on the rain case; it survives as natural dry-weather headroom (~33 % over the dry duty 6.80/7.15 m2). Rejected options: rain duty +25 % (11.3/11.9 m2) and rain feed derate (~233 t/h).

I.name: Imperfection (remapped I_new = 1 - I_old after the M3 arbitration: the spec-sheet 0.6 was written under the old inverted semantics; to confirm by a screen-product sieve test; range kept [0.1;0.9] deliberately (strict remap of the sheet range is [0.1;0.6], the wide max keeps rain-grade values reachable))
I.status: [H] Client arbitration 2026-08-10 (question 1/12): I = 0.15 adopted from literature (industrial dry vibrating screens I~0.10-0.15; Karra 1979 fixed exponent ~ classic imperfection 0.13). Supersedes the 0.4 inherited from the spec remap; to be re-fitted when a KFS product sieve test exists.

CR.5009.type: Primary crusher - SIZER CLASS selected (client 2026-08-16, CR.5009 10-expert panel Q3: twin-shaft toothed sizer supersedes the as-built toothed-roll designation; the M1 product model is unchanged, its parameters re-fit at the vendor gradation test)
CR.5009._max_feed_note: CLIENT DECISIONS 2026-08-16 (CR.5009 panel Q2+Q3): the quarry GUARANTEES max lump <= 250 mm (ripping + face scalping - to be added to the quarry works specification) and the selected sizer class positively engages that lump - supersedes the 150 mm roll-nip limit (basis of the standing alert since 2026-08-11). The alert now fires only if a feed curve implies F80 > 250 mm; NOTE the encoded quarry-target curve tail gives F80 251 mm, marginally above the guarantee - the curve top end [H] must be re-shaped to the 250 mm cap at its next revision (registered).

x80.name: Product x80 (null = follows gap; x80 = g validated 2026-08-08)

CR.5009._power_note: CLIENT DECISION 2026-08-16 (CR.5009 panel Q6): vendor standard twin-drive package accepted (2 x ~110 kW with soft starters) - restart-under-load torque by design. Absorbed duty unchanged (96.6 kW worst mode 1A; 66.5 kW mode 1B).
CR.5009._settings_note: g = 60 mm adopted 2026-08-13 (0/20-balance optimization campaign: coarser roll product preserves the 20-35 KFS band; was 40)

v.name: Rotor speed
v.status: Client arbitration 2026-08-14: v = 30 m/s adopted (was 35, reference configuration 2026-08-13). The impactor's minimum speed — last remaining zone-1 settings headroom against the 0/20 landfill: -9 800 t/y (58.4 -> 48.6 kt), KFS envelope verified compliant (in-cut 85.4 %).

CR.5011._capacity_note: Q8 CLOSED 2026-08-11 (expert book ch.4, machine documents Ochse 2026-07-17): HAZEMAG AP-S 1010 — 100 t/h nominal, 75-90 t/h real on limestone (max_capacity_tph = 90, conservative bound 75), rotor 1000x1000, max feed 400 mm, motor 132 kW; capacity bound by the rotor, not the motor. Supersedes the spec's '~125 t/h (mode A)'. Operational constraint: in mode 1B the LINE feed must drop to ~130 t/h to keep the impactor in range (the engine does not enforce line feed; check mode-1B scenarios against this)
CR.5011._settings_note: CSS 30 mm / v 35 m/s adopted 2026-08-13 (same campaign: recycle re-crushed coarse reports to KFS; low speed limits fines). Mode 1B at 250 t/h is NOT possible at these settings (impactor would exceed capacity) — irrelevant since the 0/20 balance no longer needs stock campaigns
CR.5011._capacity_basis_note: Adversarial audit 2026-08-14: the 90 t/h real capacity is a VENDOR rating (Q8, AP-S 1010 docs) — vendor tonnages are as-fed (wet). The loop check converts the dry stream to wet before comparing (previously a ~7.5 % blind spot at 7 % moisture).
CR.5011._mode_1B_note: Mode-1B setting (2026-08-14): at the reference CSS 30 the 1B loop cannot pass material below 20 mm and diverges; 18 mm restores convergence. Operations switch the CSS with the mode (pattern: RC.2 mode_F_gap_mm).

BF.5101.type: Reclaim feeders (pair BF.5101 + BF.5102, 100 T/h each — PFD REV18)

SR.5105.type: Reclaim screen 6 mm, single deck (PFD REV18; the spec's 15/5 double deck is SUPERSEDED — decision 2026-08-12)

a.name: Aperture (FeedLime cut: oversize a/20 = FeedLime, undersize 0/a -> AgLime loop)

SR.5111.type: First 1.7 mm closing screen, OPEN circuit (PFD REV18: undersize = AgLime, oversize -> CR.5113)
SR.5111._purchase_min_note: CLIENT DECISION 2026-08-15 (error-hunt M-1, option 1 of 3): re-quoted by the FULL VSMA factor method (scripts/vsma_factor_sizing.py) - worst factor duty 1.65 m2 (2C, measured/1A; the model said 1.42) -> x1.25 -> 2.1 m2 (was 1.8). The vendor bed-depth sizing at 100 t/h WET still GOVERNS over this cut-duty minimum (sheet caveat unchanged).
SR.5111._loop_rating_note: BC.5110/BC.5116 conveyors rated 60 T/h (PFD REV18) — alert when the loop feed exceeds it

SR.5115.type: Second 1.7 mm closing screen, CLOSED loop with CR.5113 (PFD REV18: undersize joins AgLime, oversize recycles to the crusher)
SR.5115._purchase_min_note: Error-hunt M-1 disposition 2026-08-15: the VSMA factor method gives a LOWER worst duty here (10.61 m2 quarry/1B/2C -> 13.3 with margin) than the published model-based minimum 19.1 m2 (its ~78 % oversize feed earns a high VSMA oversize factor). RULE APPLIED: an issued purchase floor is never weakened without a dedicated client arbitration - 19.1 m2 RETAINED (conservative), factor-method figure disclosed on the sheet. Also fixes the audit's M-2 note (the model worst 15.72 m2 x1.25 = 19.65 slightly exceeded 19.1; the retained floor is now formally the CLIENT-DECIDED value, and the vendor bed-depth sizing at the 2C bed load governs).

DY.03._capacity_note: Client 2026-08-13: dryer capacity limit = 30 t/h AT THE OUTLET (dried product, 0.5 % moisture) = 32.1 t/h wet feed at 7 % (30 x 0.995 / 0.93). The engine cap max_capacity_tph checks the wet FEED.

S_att.name: Attrition per pass [H] (refitted after the M3 arbitration + imperfection remap; spec sheet default was 0.206)

ML.26._product_curve_note: Vendor abaque slot (golden rule 2): set to {"curve_pct": {mesh_mm: cumulative %}, "interpolation": "linear"|"log"} to replace hypotheses H-M7-1/2 with the vendor product curve
ML.26._model_note: Model M7 structure VALIDATED by literature (Thiere, TU Freiberg PhD 2020, pilot toothed double-roll tests): two-component product (gap-driven compression PSD + fines sub-collective), sub-gap bypass, reduction ratio ~4. The S_att constant could be refined to the published gap/feed-dependent form S_att = s0*(F80/g); a vendor product_curve_table remains the best upgrade

coupe.name: Cut size (Q6 CLOSED 2026-08-11: d50c = 0.65 x d97 = 65 um per expert book ch.11, Stokes equilibrium; was 100)

eta_cl.name: Extraction efficiency [H] (literature: real quarry air classifiers recover 50-65% at finer cuts; 0.75 is a defensible design midpoint for an easy ~100 um cut, flagged optimistic)

SP.36._max_airflow_note: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-16 (benchmark improvement Q4, client option 2): SP.36 is re-specified as a FULL-STREAM dynamic classifier (feed = the whole 0/1.5 fines stream, 13.6-23.3 t/h; Ventoplex-class with INTERNAL fan) - the external 420 m3/h fan decided under PD-3 (2026-08-15) no longer has an object and its purchase is CANCELLED; the CL.38 product cyclone is WITHDRAWN from the purchase list (internal recirculation; the polishing bag filter remains as the circuit vent). The engine's Q_air remains the process-model cut lever; the air circuit is vendor-internal. HONESTY CEILING kept on record: the natural sub-65-um content of the fines is 0.60-0.66 % - the full-stream machine harvests AT MOST ~430 t/y of UltraFin (vs 284 today); kt-scale quartz-free output would require a grinding circuit (rejected by the client this round).

RC.1.type: Smooth double-roll crusher, stage 1 (C1 study variant — replaces ML.26; NOT adopted, as-built remains the default)

comp_lam.name: Compression [H] (smooth rolls: single-pass nip, low over-grinding vs toothed 4.11)

n_comp.name: RR slope n of the compression component [H] (smooth-roll product steepness; vendor gradation test pending)

S_att.name: Attrition per pass [H] (smooth rolls: no tooth attrition, surface abrasion only)

RC.1._product_curve_note: Vendor abaque slot (golden rule 2): a smooth-roll gradation test on WANKOE 6/20 fixes n_comp and S_att before any purchase.
RC.1._model_note: Model M7 with per-machine overrides (comp_lam, S_att, m7_n_comp). C1 design basis: docs/design/zone13-redesign/design-basis.md + panel-candidates.md (panel round 1, client-validated 2026-08-14).
RC.1._capacity_note: Client arbitration 2026-08-14: purchase spec 32 t/h (panel sizing was 29). Covers the full-dryer extension on BOTH feed curves — measured 28.9 t/h and quarry-target 29.7 t/h (the 29 t/h spec was exceeded on the quarry variant, D4 verification finding).
RC.1._capacity_basis_note: DRY-solids loop capacity by definition: these purchase specs were derived from the engine's dry loop loads (zone 1.3 runs at 0.5 % outlet moisture, so wet/dry differ by < 0.5 %). Audit 2026-08-14.

RC.2.type: Smooth double-roll crusher, stage 2, TWO parallel units (client 2026-08-14: 2nd unit installed to serve the 60 kt/y fines objective; purchase spec includes mode-F capability = minimum gap 1.5 mm, vendor to confirm)
RC.2._capacity_note: CLIENT DECISION 2026-08-15 (error-hunt PD-4, option 1 of 3): per-unit purchase capacity raised 22 -> 25 t/h (standard vendor size step). The mode-F operating point (feed 25.05, load 44.0 t/h on the x2 grid) had been encoded at EXACTLY 100 % of 2x22 on a grid NOT converged for that output (x4 -> 44.4 t/h), with zero gap-drift allowance (gap 1.6 -> 44.95) and +/-7.5 % load swing per +/-10 % on the untested comp_lam [H]. 2x25 = ~12 % headroom covering all three. Mode-F feed UNCHANGED at 25.05 (rejected: feed derate to ~24.5, and doing both). The vendor gradation test remains the comp_lam arbiter.

n_comp.name: RR slope n of the compression component [H]

RC.2._product_curve_note: Vendor abaque slot (golden rule 2): roll capacity at 3.4 mm gap to be confirmed by vendor trial.
RC.2._model_note: max_capacity_tph is PER UNIT. No physical feed split is modelled: m7's product PSD is flow-independent and Bond power uses the total flow, so splitting across units in service is mathematically equivalent (audit 2026-08-14 clarification of the earlier 'splits the feed' wording).
RC.2._extension_note: Client arbitration 2026-08-14 (fines-objective config, option 1): BOTH units installed. Mode G runs 1 unit at the throttled feed or 2 at full dryer; mode F needs both (load ~44 t/h at its feed). Purchase spec: rolls capable of closing to 1.5 mm (mode-F gap) — vendor gradation test to confirm.
RC.2._capacity_basis_note: DRY-solids loop capacity by definition: these purchase specs were derived from the engine's dry loop loads (zone 1.3 runs at 0.5 % outlet moisture, so wet/dry differ by < 0.5 %). Audit 2026-08-14.
RC.2._mode_F_note: Mode-F gap = 1.5 mm (client design 2026-08-14): required so the diverted 2/3.75 band is nipped instead of circulating (engine: 147 t/h runaway load at 2.8 mm vs 37-44 t/h workable at 1.5).

SC.A.type: Double-deck RECYCLE screen 8 / 3.75 mm (C1 study variant, client arbitration 2026-08-14: 2+2 arrangement — recycle cuts on SC.A, product cuts on SC.B)

SC.B.type: Double-deck PRODUCT screen 2 / 1.5 mm (C1 study variant: deck 1 = grits bottom cut, D6-critical; deck 2 = fines top cut; both critical decks in favorable position — the 2+2 rationale)
SC.B._purchase_min_note: CLIENT DECISION 2026-08-15 (error-hunt M-1, option 1 of 3): fine-screen purchase minima re-quoted by the FULL VSMA factor method (scripts/vsma_factor_sizing.py) - the engine M4 model carries no composition factors and under-sizes SC.B's low-half-size feeds (17-20 % passing a/2) by ~25-30 %. Worst factor-method duty across measured/quarry x 1A/1B x G/F: 5.85 m2 (d1, 1B x F) / 5.95 m2 (d2, mode F mass-pinned) -> x1.25 -> 7.4 / 7.5 m2 (was 6.5 / 5.6 model-based). Vendor bed-depth sizing verifies; the RPN-252 panel requirements are unchanged.

a1.name: Aperture 1 (grits bottom cut; 2.0 protects the D6 <2 mm <= 15 %)

a2.name: Aperture 2 (fines top cut; 1.5 protects the 0/1.5 fines spec + redirect eligibility)

SC.B._routing_note: Client arbitration 2026-08-14: the 1.5/2 sliver (SC.B deck-2 oversize) is REGROUND through RC.2 ('regrind'); 'extract' keeps it as a separate Sliver 1.5/2 product. Two-position diverter in the plant design — reversible in operation; to be confirmed by the vendor gradation test (D6 margin 1.4 pts under regrind).
SC.B._grits_diverter_note: Client design addition 2026-08-14: a second two-position diverter on the SC.B deck-1 oversize (the 2/3.75 grits stream) routes it either to the grits product chain (mode G) or into the RC.2 regrind circuit alongside the sliver (mode F — fines campaign when grits demand is filled). The position is driven by default_scenario.zone_1_3_mode.

Wi.name: Bond work index
Wi.status: Q2 CLOSED 2026-08-11 [ref.]: 12.54 kWh/t confirmed by expert book ch.13 — Fontaine value (Belgian limestone), consistent with measured limestone range 12.6-13.9 kWh/t (Todorovic 2017). The kWh/short-ton hypothesis (13.8) is REJECTED; the spec ch.9 ~116 kW remains a spec-side artefact. Site Bond test still listed as a calibration trigger (book ch.13)

b_j.status: [H] literature default. FLAG (2026-08-08): A*b=48 is mid-hard; JKTech database trends put SOFT limestone at A*b~60-80 (b~1.0-1.4 at A=60) - current 0.8 is a conservative hard-side choice

I_dry.name: Screen imperfection (dry)
I_dry.status: [H] Client arbitration 2026-08-10 (question 1/12): I = 0.15 adopted from literature (industrial dry vibrating screens I~0.10-0.15; Karra 1979 fixed exponent ~ classic imperfection 0.13). Supersedes the 0.4 inherited from the spec remap; to be re-fitted when a KFS product sieve test exists.

m7_n_comp.status: hypothesis H-M7-1 - [H] refitted on reference case 9.3 after the M3 arbitration + imperfection remap (2026-08-08), exact match, to confirm by trial

m7_n_att.status: hypothesis H-M7-2 - [H] refitted on reference case 9.3 after the M3 arbitration + imperfection remap (2026-08-08), exact match, to confirm by trial

I_rain.name: Fine screen imperfection under rain
I_rain.status: [H] spec M3 (up to ~0.9). REQUALIFIED 2026-08-15 (client, rain-week study): wet screening at 1.7 mm is PHYSICALLY IMPOSSIBLE - rain forces mode 2B as PHYSICS, not policy, so I_rain is reachable ONLY in the audit branch rain_forces_mode_2B=false, whose AgLime result is DIRECTIONAL and never an operating case

b_cyclone.name: CL.38 cyclone inlet width
b_cyclone.status: design assumption adopted 2026-08-11 from expert book ch.12: D = 0.7 m, b = 0.2D = 0.14 m (Stairmand high-efficiency), Ne = 5, v_in = 15 m/s -> d50 = 4.2 um; sub-4 um tail leaves with the cleaned air and needs a polishing bag filter (equipment NOT in the flowsheet). Vendor drawing still to confirm

bottom_interval_ratio.name: Bottom size interval lower-bound ratio (rep. size = mesh/sqrt(ratio))

wet_capacity_factor.name: Screen basic-capacity derating factor under rain (outdoor screens)
wet_capacity_factor.status: [H] spec M3/SR.5115 narrative ('capacity drops when wet') quantified as a hypothesis, to confirm. SCOPE requalified 2026-08-15 (client, rain-week study): applies to the cuts that REMAIN FEASIBLE wet - 20/35 mm (SR.5007) and 6 mm (SR.5105) - as an area derating; the 1.7 mm cut is not derated but IMPOSSIBLE under rain (mode 2B is physics); the zone-1.3 SC.A/SC.B cuts sit BEHIND the dryer at 0.5 % moisture and are never derated

engine._comment: Numerical engine settings - adjustable without reprogramming.
engine._grid_refinement_note: Client arbitration 2026-08-14 (numerical-robustness study, action 5): the computation grid inserts 1 geometric midpoint per spec-sieve interval (57 meshes) — converged to < 0.05 pt of KFS Yield vs x4; the spec sieve series stays the PRESENTATION format. Set to 1 to reproduce spec-era (ch.9) numerics.

feed_product.comment: Pivot feed: belt-cut PSD MEASURED at the primary crusher outlet on 2026-08-08 (raw data: data/feed_measurements/2026-08-08-belt-cut.json). Measured range 19-200 mm; fine tail < 19 mm and top size completed by hypotheses H-FEED-1/H-FEED-2 (see data/measured_feed_curve.json, rebuild with scripts/build_feed_curve_from_measurement.py). Model checks: d50 32.3 mm (measured 32), d80 180.6 mm (measured 180).

moisture_pct._rain_week_note: This is the GLOBAL photo moisture: scenario.py gives the zone-1.2 reclaim and zone-1.3 FeedLime streams this same value (no per-stream moisture yet - model-improvement item). The client's porous-stone RAIN-WEEK set (2026-08-15, [H] pending the ABSORPTION TEST on samples: quarry feed 12 %, reclaimed 0/20 stock 15 %, FeedLime 6/20 stock 11 %, drainage back to 7 % over 5-7 days) lives data-first in docs/design/moisture/rain-week-scenario.json and is read as a composite of per-zone photos by scripts/rain_week_study.py

wet_density_tm3.status: to be confirmed - reserved, not used by the engine yet

UCS_MPa.status: Client arbitration 2026-08-15 (soft-rock study, choice 1): rock class = very soft limestone, rippable, no blasting - UCS reference 20 MPa, envelope 15-30 MPa (supersedes the reserved geology DP9442 slot). CASE DISCRIMINATOR ONLY, never a formula input (rule 2026-08-11): hardness enters the engine via Wi (M2) and A_j.b_j (M5), whose DEFAULTS ARE UNCHANGED pending the drop-weight/gradation tests - the soft-rock coefficient set lives in docs/design/soft-rock/soft-rock-scenario.json as an overrides scenario

friability.status: geology - reserved, not used by the engine yet

envelope._note: KFS 30/55/15 envelope - three %-passing control thresholds (interpretation validated 2026-08-08). The spec's '15%' is the above-cut limit: a strict 15% total out-of-cut tolerance would always fail (Karra screening leaves ~43% out of 20/35), so max_out_of_cut_tol_pct is null (superseded by the envelope).

AgLime._criterion_note: Client decision 2026-08-12 (zone-1.2 doc question Q8): acceptance criterion >= 95 % passing 1.7 mm, i.e. max 5 % out of cut. No contractual AgLime spec existed before; this is the project criterion

FeedLime grits._envelope_note: D6 grits spec (client, zone-1.3 design basis 2026-08-14): <2 mm <= 15 %, >4 mm <= 5 %

Sliver 1.5/2._note: C1 study variant only, and only when SC.B oversize_routing = 'extract'. Client arbitration 2026-08-14: default routing is REGRIND (sliver returns to RC.2), so this product is normally absent.

stockpile_capacities_t._note: Yard capacities from the NACO/Carmeuse PFDs (2026-08-12) — data only, engine does not enforce them yet; flagged for the seasonal-swing check (zone-1.2 planning found ~16.4 kt FeedLime swing vs 6 kt capacity)

FeedLime grits 2-4._note: Client 2026-08-13 (evening): back to the FIRM 40 000 t/y — the 44 400 optimization variant remains available as a scenario, not the default

FeedLime fines 0/1.5._note: Client ruling 2026-08-14: 60 000 t/y is a PRODUCTION OBJECTIVE (the market must be served), no longer a passive co-product cap. The planning adds mode-F fines-campaign hours to close the gap left by the mode-G co-production.

default_scenario._rain_forces_mode_2B_note: REQUALIFIED 2026-08-15 (client, rain-week study): this forcing is PHYSICS, not an operating policy - WET SCREENING AT 1.7 mm IS IMPOSSIBLE (blinding), so rain means ZERO AgLime, full stop. The zone-1.3 SC.B 2/1.5 product cuts are UNAFFECTED (behind the dryer at 0.5 %); the 6 mm and 20/35 mm cuts stay feasible wet with the wet_capacity_factor derating. false remains selectable ONLY as an audit branch (I_rain, DIRECTIONAL result), never an operating case. Rain-week stock moistures: docs/design/moisture/rain-week-scenario.json

flow_rates_tph._mode_1B_note: CLIENT DECISION 2026-08-15 (error-hunt PD-1, option 1): re-bisected on the ADOPTED QUARRY-TARGET CURVE so the CR.5011 90 t/h WET vendor guarantee holds in ALL circumstances - 172.0 t/h wet gives 89.7 t/h wet on the quarry curve and 83.2 on the measured curve, CLEAN on grids x2/x3/x4 (no operating point encoded at exactly 100 % of capacity - PD-4 lesson). Supersedes the 2026-08-14 bisection (186.1, measured curve only, which put the quarry-curve load at 97.1 > 90). At the mode-1B CSS (CR.5011.mode_1B_x80_mm).

1.1._note: 1 shift, 6d/7 — Saturday extension decided by the client 2026-08-13 (Q7 securing lever; was 2000 h at 5d/7)

default_scenario._variant_note: C1 reference configuration (client 2026-08-14, fines-objective update): RC.1 + TWO RC.2 units, SC.A 8/3.75 + SC.B 2/1.5, sliver regrind, grits diverter (modes G/F). Mode G runs the dryer at its full 32.1 t/h wet limit (RC.2 33.2/44); mode F (fines campaign, RC.2 gap 1.5) at 25.05 t/h wet — both RC.2 units exactly at capacity. 'as-built' remains selectable. [H] coefficients pending the vendor gradation test.
default_scenario._flow_rates_note: CLIENT RULE (ratified 2026-08-14): every flow_rates_tph entry is the TOTAL flow — WET basis, dry solids PLUS water — as belt-weighed. zone_1_1_feed 250 and zone_1_2_reclaim 100 are wet by this rule; zone_1_3_feedlime is wet too (the dryer sheet converts). The engine converts to dry solids at each zone boundary (q_dry = q_wet x (1 - moisture/100)); internal stream 'q' values are dry solids for conservation, and PRESENTED rates are quoted in total (wet) flow unless explicitly labeled dry.
default_scenario._zone_1_3_mode_note: Two zone-1.3 operating modes (client 2026-08-14): 'G' = grits production (2/3.75 to product); 'F' = fines campaign (2/3.75 diverted to RC.2 regrind, RC.2 at mode_F_gap_mm). The annual plan splits the hours between modes so BOTH the firm grits target and the fines market land exactly.

commercial_rules._note: Client rules governing how the planning closes the commercial balance
commercial_rules._020_conversion_note: CLIENT RULE 2026-08-16 (supersedes the landfill disposal of 2026-08-13 as the DEFAULT): the 0/20 excess is MANDATORILY sold as AgLime or FeedLime - never landfilled, never sold crude. Planning route: additional dedicated 2C conversion hours turn the excess into AgLime through the zone-1.2 loop (the FeedLime route stays available if the AgLime channel cannot absorb - dry-season capacity guard applies, any unconvertible remainder falls back to the landfill accounting WITH an alert). The AgLime sold through this rule comes ON TOP of the 135 kt market cap - a client-ruled market extension, reported as its own labeled sales line.
commercial_rules._020_note: Client 2026-08-13: there is NO market for crude 0/20. Landfill is now the FALLBACK ONLY (rule above off, or conversion capacity exhausted): the remainder goes to LANDFILL as a NET FINANCIAL LOSS, alerted, never a sale.
commercial_rules._auto_mode_1B_note: Client rule 2026-08-14: KFS is NEVER over-produced — when the 0/20 demand would drive zone 1.1 beyond the KFS-target hours, mode-1A hours land the KFS target EXACTLY and the 0/20 deficit is produced by dedicated mode-1B hours (no KFS: 20-35 recirculated into CR.5011 at zone_1_1_feed_mode_1B / mode_1B_x80_mm). Toggleable; off = legacy max() behavior with an overproduction alert.
commercial_rules._aglime_2c_note: Client rule (2026-08-13: 'producing lime is never a problem, separate campaign' — wired 2026-08-14 after the C1 adoption dried up the fines redirect): when the 2A co-production plus the fines redirect leave the AgLime market cap unserved, zone 1.2 runs DEDICATED mode-2C campaigns (everything reclaimed leaves as AgLime) to produce the complement. Toggleable; campaign hours count toward the zone-1.2 ceiling.

kfs_yield.definition: KFS Yield = whole KFS product stream (BC.5013 to stock, wet) / zone-1.1 PIVOT feed (wet, measured downstream of CR.5003). Always reported WITH the real KFS 20/35 PSD (in-cut / below / above).
kfs_yield.target: dynamic: required-for-zero-landfill = KFS / (KFS + downstream 0/20 demand); alert when realized < required
kfs_yield.status: Client definition, 4 questions arbitrated 2026-08-14 (numerator = whole product stream; wet/wet; pivot denominator; dynamic target)

_meta.purpose: ELECTRICITY-ONLY OPEX model — client arbitration 2026-08-15, 4 choices: (1) PERIMETER = process machines + materials handling + dryer ELECTRICAL auxiliaries; the dryer BURNER BU.04 is FUEL-fired and excluded from electricity (its thermal MWh reported separately); (2) POWER BASIS = ABSORBED power: engine-modeled machines use the per-mode photo P_net_kW / eta_m; non-modeled drives use TYPICAL installed ratings [H] x absorption_factor; (3) HOURS from run_required_hours (hours follow the targets), split per zone and operating mode; a consumer runs only during the mode-hour buckets listed in its 'modes' key; (4) OUTPUT = kWh only (annual kWh by machine / zone / mode / total + kWh/t per sold product), no euros.

consumer_schema.zone: planning zone whose hours drive the consumer (1.1 / 1.2 / 1.3)
consumer_schema.modes: operating-mode hour buckets the consumer runs in — zone 1.1: 1A, 1B; zone 1.2: 2A = dry-season loop hours, 2B = rain-season bypass hours, 2C = dedicated AgLime campaigns; zone 1.3: G, F. Client arbitration 2026-08-15: the zone-1.2 loop machines (SR.5111, CR.5113, SR.5115) and SR.5105 run in BOTH the 2A and 2C hours.
consumer_schema.basis: 'engine' = absorbed power read from the per-mode scenario photo (P_net_kW / eta_m, models M2/M5); 'typical_rating' = installed_kW (typical nameplate, [H]) x absorption_factor
consumer_schema.installed_kW: typical motor nameplate rating [H] (typical_rating basis only)
